title: 1958 AHSME Problem 36
statement: The sides of a triangle are \(30,\) \(70,\) and \(80\) units. If an altitude is dropped upon the side of length \(80,\) the larger segment cut off on this side is:

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the segment adjacent to the side of length \(30.\) If the altitude has length \(h,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} 30^2-x^2&=h^2,\\ h^2&=70^2-(80-x)^2. \end{aligned} \] Cancelling \(x^2\) and solving gives \(x=15.\) The other segment is \(80-15=65,\) which is the larger one.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the altitude divide the side of length \(80\) into \(x\) and \(80-x\)
Equate the two expressions for the square of the altitude
